note: The base rate is the whole point of this act: `bearMarkets` divided by `years` gives the odds that any given year contains the start of a 20%-plus fall, which is the score a person gets for shouting "crash" every January and doing no other work. Rounded for readability.
source: Bear-market count: Ned Davis Research / Hartford Funds, "10 Things You Should Know About Bear Markets" — 27 bear markets in the S&P 500 between 1928 and 2024 (and 28 bull markets). Corrections of 10 percent or more are roughly annual on the same count. The "market can stay irrational" line is attributed to Keynes everywhere and appears nowhere in Keynes; the earliest print attribution traces to A. Gary Shilling in Forbes, 1993.

quote.text: The market can remain irrational longer than you can remain solvent.
quote.actually: Nobody can find it in Keynes. The earliest printed version is A. Gary Shilling, Forbes, 1993.
